newsitem.title: USA: Jesse Jackson's half-brother found guilty.
newsitem.headline: Jesse Jackson's half-brother found guilty.

text.p: The half-brother of civil rights leader Jesse Jackson has been convicted for a second time of a murder-for-hire plot along with drug and racketeering charges, prosecutors said Friday.

Noah Robinson, a former Chicago restaurant owner and successful businessman, and four high-ranking leaders of a street gang were found guilty Thursday on all counts. The defendants could be sentenced to life in prison.

Prosecutors argued in Robinson's second trial, which Jackson attended occasionally, that he sought to become the "godfather" of the "El Rukns" street gang by arranging drug connections for the gang. They also said Robinson told a gang member to kill a former boyhood friend turned enemy.

Convictions in 1991 of Robinson and three El Rukn leaders were thrown out by a federal judge after turncoat gang members testifying for the prosecution were found to be taking drugs and engaging in sex while in protective custody. Prosecutors secured testimony from other gang members in the second trial.
